sections.heading: Who Tharun Subramanya is
sections.text: Tharun Subramanya is an applied machine learning engineer working on industrial systems, edge IoT, and robotics. He holds a Master of Science in Artificial Intelligence from the University of Michigan-Dearborn, completed in May 2026 with a GPA of 3.74 out of 4.00. His background combines Industrial and Production Engineering with applied AI.

sections.heading: What he works on
sections.text: His applied machine learning work spans CAN-bus fault classification, vibration-based condition monitoring, drift-aware edge predictive maintenance, and computer-vision perception pipelines. He is currently extending that sensor-level diagnostic foundation toward robotics and physical AI systems.

sections.heading: How he approaches evaluation
sections.text: His work is consistently grounded in data-quality validation and session-held-out evaluation rather than inflated benchmark numbers. Reported metrics are revised downward whenever a higher figure cannot be defended. Splits are held out by recording session, by video, or by group so that neighbouring samples never leak across an evaluation boundary.

sections.heading: Career direction
sections.text: He is moving from sensor and time-series machine learning toward robotics and robot learning. The bridge is data quality: deciding automatically which sensor data, or which demonstration, is trustworthy enough to train on. He is open to roles in applied AI, industrial IoT, edge AI, and robotics.

sections.heading: Why the industrial engineering degree matters
sections.text: The Industrial and Production Engineering degree supplies manufacturing process knowledge that a pure computer science background does not: statistical quality control, metrology and measurement systems, control engineering, mechatronics, and CNC and robotics laboratory work. It means he understands a fabrication or production floor as an engineer rather than as a visitor, which is directly relevant to industrial robotics, manufacturing quality engineering, and digital-twin modelling of facilities.

sections.heading: CANalyse Edge overview
sections.text: CANalyse Edge is a CAN signal decoding and diagnostic validation service, currently in progress. Stack: Python, python-can, cantools, scikit-learn, FastAPI, pytest, GitHub Actions.

sections.heading: CANalyse Edge decoding pipeline
sections.text: Engineered a CAN and CAN-FD diagnostic pipeline decoding raw frames into named engineering signals through DBC mapping. Records timing, DLC, and signal-range checks as data-quality evidence on every validation run.

sections.heading: CANalyse Edge model and evaluation
sections.text: Derived rolling signal-window features feeding a Random Forest component-condition model. Held out 3 unseen recording sessions of 6, so neighbouring windows never leak across the evaluation split. This session-level holdout is the point: random splits on windowed sensor data leak, and the resulting accuracy is fiction.

sections.heading: CANalyse Edge diagnostic API
sections.text: Exposed results through a SOVD-inspired FastAPI service serving entity, component-health, fault, data, and operation resources, with a dashboard supporting issue triage and root-cause inspection.

sections.heading: CANalyse Edge testing and datasets
sections.text: Automated a pytest regression suite in continuous integration. Curated a public dataset registry covering ReCAN, ROAD, Scania Component X, and Q-Motion, under a validation protocol that reports simulator output as synthetic smoke tests rather than as real results.

sections.heading: DARE-PM overview
sections.text: DARE-PM is drift-aware edge predictive maintenance with out-of-distribution monitoring, completed April 2026. Stack: Python, scikit-learn, One-Class SVM, ADWIN, MQTT, Docker, InfluxDB, Grafana. Built as coursework for CIS 489 Edge Computing at the University of Michigan-Dearborn.

sections.heading: DARE-PM feature extraction
sections.text: Constructed an edge predictive-maintenance system extracting 14 time-domain and frequency-domain features every 0.1 seconds from vibration and acoustic streams, on-device.

sections.heading: DARE-PM drift detection
sections.text: Applied One-Class SVM novelty detection, an out-of-distribution detector fitted on nominal data alone, combined with ADWIN concept-drift diagnosis. The ADWIN stage separates true distribution shift from benign environmental variation, which prevents needless retraining.

sections.heading: DARE-PM results
sections.text: Cut false model adaptations from 49.87 percent to under 1 percent while sustaining F1 up to 0.80. That false-alarm rate is the characteristic failure mode of naive drift detectors. Reached 88.4 percent data reduction and 3.8 millisecond inference latency, validated across 48 controlled experiments.

sections.heading: DARE-PM deployment
sections.text: Deployed containerized Docker and MQTT services with continuous performance monitoring through InfluxDB and Grafana.

sections.heading: DARE-PM buzz squeak and rattle reframe
sections.text: Reframed under faculty mentorship toward vehicle buzz, squeak and rattle detection. The extension replaces single-detector drift with a multi-signal arbitration layer: per-feature ADWIN, rolling confidence, and cross-sensor majority voting. The reason is that ADWIN alone cannot distinguish a genuine fault from a benign environmental shift, so a second signal is needed to arbitrate before anything reaches the controller.

documents.title: Vehicle Type and Speed Pattern Recognition

sections.heading: Vehicle Type and Speed Pattern Recognition overview
sections.text: A traffic perception pipeline for vehicle detection, tracking, four-class classification, and calibrated speed estimation, completed April 2025. Stack: Python, OpenCV, TensorFlow and Keras, convolutional neural networks.

sections.heading: Vehicle recognition training and split
sections.text: Trained convolutional neural networks on 17,760 labelled vehicle crops under a group-level split by video, so that no same-vehicle frames were shared across training and validation. Reached approximately 85 percent binary accuracy and above 79 percent multi-class validation accuracy.

sections.heading: Vehicle tracking and speed estimation
sections.text: Implemented MOG2 background subtraction, contour filtering, centroid tracking, and multi-frame voting to stabilize vehicle identities. Estimated speed from centroid displacement, frame rate, and lane-width calibration.

sections.heading: Automatic Number Plate Recognition overview
sections.text: A perception pipeline and robustness testing project for automatic number plate recognition, completed March 2024. Stack: YOLOv5, PyTorch, OpenCV, Tesseract, Albumentations, Docker, AWS EC2.

sections.heading: ANPR dataset and robustness testing
sections.text: Curated more than 12,000 annotated images from the OpenALPR Benchmark and Kaggle. Generated perturbed variants through rotation, brightness and contrast shifts, and synthetic occlusion, to test detection robustness under degraded imaging conditions.

sections.heading: ANPR detection and OCR
sections.text: Fine-tuned YOLOv5 for plate detection, reaching 95 percent mAP. Assembled an OCR stage from OpenCV preprocessing, a Keras convolutional character segmenter with pytesseract, and regular-expression correction.

sections.heading: ANPR deployment and results
sections.text: Containerized detection and OCR in Docker and deployed a Flask service on AWS EC2 through a CI/CD pipeline. Sustained inference under 50 milliseconds per image at 89 percent end-to-end accuracy, cutting manual logging effort by 85 percent.

documents.title: Smart Brake and Wheel-End Condition Monitor

sections.heading: Smart Brake and Wheel-End Condition Monitor overview
sections.text: A physics-first brake and wheel-end diagnostic system, currently in progress, built with a collaborator. Stack: Python, NumPy, scikit-learn, pytest, ruff, GitHub Actions. Tharun owns the thermal simulation, drag-torque injection and torque-inversion work.

sections.heading: Brake rotor thermal simulation
sections.text: Modelled rotor thermal behaviour with a lumped-capacitance simulator incorporating speed-dependent convection and radiation. Injected residual caliper drag torque across four severity levels, over a dual-wheel front-left and front-right configuration.

sections.heading: Brake torque inversion from cooling curves
sections.text: Devised a Newtonian cooling-curve feature extractor that inverts drag torque from the cooling asymptote rather than classifying a black-box signature. Recovers torque within roughly 5 percent of ground truth on severe-drag cases. Physical inversion was chosen over classification deliberately: an interpretable torque estimate carries a diagnostic story to a service engineer that a classifier confidence score cannot.

sections.heading: Brake project testing
sections.text: Guarded by an 18-test suite gated in continuous integration through ruff, pytest and coverage reporting.

documents.title: Edge Sensing Pipeline and Serverless Digital Twin

sections.heading: Edge sensing pipeline overview
sections.text: An end-to-end telemetry chain running on physical Raspberry Pi hardware. DHT sensors publish over a Mosquitto MQTT broker to a Python subscriber, are persisted to storage, and are visualised for trend inspection.

sections.heading: Serverless digital twin and alerting
sections.text: Extended the pipeline into a serverless digital twin on AWS IoT Core, routing threshold breaches through Lambda to SES email alerting, running against real hardware rather than a simulator.

sections.heading: Lessons from deploying on real hardware
sections.text: Each layer was validated independently, sensor to broker to subscriber to storage to alert, before end-to-end testing, because going straight to integration doubles the time spent locating which link broke. Real failure modes encountered: silent region mismatches between IoT Core, Lambda and SES; certificate filename drift in authentication scripts; and a unit-conversion error that tripped every threshold while passing casual tests.

documents.title: Supply Chain Risk Data Pipeline and Predictive Analytics

sections.heading: Supply chain risk pipeline overview
sections.text: An end-to-end predictive pipeline over more than 180,000 supply-chain orders across 53 attributes, built May to July 2026. Covers data cleaning, validation, preprocessing and model development. Stack: Python, pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn.

sections.heading: Supply chain feature engineering
sections.text: Engineered shipment, temporal, operational and categorical features using leakage-safe preprocessing for late-delivery prediction. Reduced one-hot encoded dimensionality from over 64,000 features to 339 through high-cardinality feature optimisation and data-modelling decisions.

sections.heading: Supply chain evaluation and threshold tuning
sections.text: Evaluated precision, recall, F1 and ROC-AUC. Raised late-risk recall from 57.5 percent to 78.8 percent through decision-threshold tuning, settling on a threshold of 0.40 at a precision of 66.1 percent using logistic regression. The trade is deliberate: for a late-delivery warning, a missed late shipment costs more than a false alarm someone can dismiss.

sections.heading: Used car price forecasting overview

sections.heading: Used car modelling and results
sections.text: Raised R-squared from 0.68 to 0.80 and cut mean absolute error by 12 percent using stacked regression over Random Forest, gradient boosting and XGBoost. Engineered predictive features including vehicle age, mileage per year and fuel type.

sections.heading: Used car pipeline and delivery

sections.heading: Credit card fraud detection overview
sections.text: A fraud classification project over 284,000 transactions with a 0.17 percent fraud rate, built August to October 2023. Earlier applied machine learning work, predating the sensor and edge focus.

sections.heading: Fraud detection modelling
sections.text: Optimised XGBoost with Bayesian hyperparameter tuning, reaching 97 percent precision at 89 percent recall. Applied SMOTE balancing to lift minority-class recall by 20 percent without degrading precision. Benchmarked against logistic regression, Random Forest and a multilayer perceptron, which validated XGBoost as the strongest model on this data.

sections.heading: Fraud detection deployment and impact
sections.text: Deployed the model as a Dockerised Flask API serving predictions under 200 milliseconds in a test environment. The associated 1.2 million dollar annual loss figure is a simulated estimate from the dataset, not a measured business outcome.

documents.title: LLM, generative AI and retrieval work

sections.heading: Chappie, the retrieval system running on this site
sections.text: Chappie is a retrieval-augmented generation system Tharun built over his own CV, projects, education and skills. It runs entirely in the visitor's browser on GitHub Pages, with no server, no API key and no cold start. Retrieval is Okapi BM25 over a prebuilt index, with query expansion and same-document damping, and a full question is answered in roughly five milliseconds.

sections.heading: How Chappie is guarded
sections.text: Six gates run in order of cost: input hygiene, prompt-injection screening, out-of-distribution scope detection, an evidence floor applied after retrieval, and citation integrity checked on the way out. Answering is extractive, meaning sentences are quoted from the indexed source rather than paraphrased by a generative model, which makes a fabricated claim structurally impossible rather than merely unlikely.

sections.heading: How Chappie is evaluated
sections.text: A 69-case evaluation suite across four groups runs in headless Chromium against the real page on every push, and blocks the deployment on regression. It reports attack success rate and false refusal rate, the second being the measure most projects skip. Both currently sit at zero.

sections.heading: The generative answering path and LLM API integration
sections.text: The generative path is implemented and ships disabled by default. A FastAPI service deployable to Azure Container Apps holds the model key server-side, receives the question together with the already-retrieved passages, and returns a generated answer that may cite only passages that were actually retrieved. Citation validation runs on both the server and the client, so a hallucinated source is rejected rather than displayed.

sections.heading: Ingestion pipeline behind the retrieval system
sections.text: An offline Python pipeline chunks Markdown source documents on their headings, tokenises and stems them with a stemmer mirrored exactly in the browser, computes BM25 term statistics, and emits a single static index file. Continuous integration fails the build if the committed index has drifted out of date with the source documents.

sections.heading: Generative AI and LLM tooling
sections.text: Tharun's AI framework skills are Hugging Face Transformers, LangChain and LlamaIndex, and he lists OpenAI and Anthropic among the LLM tooling he works with. He is working through a self-directed generative AI and LLM track covering Hugging Face, LangChain and retrieval-augmented generation.
